html:
The Toba-Enenlhet, also called the Toba-Maskoy, are an Indigenous people of the Paraguayan Chaco in Paraguay. They are not the same as the Qom (Toba) of Argentina; the shared name is a confusion of outsiders.

Their language belongs to the Enlhet-Enenlhet family, with those of the Angaité, the Enxet and the Sanapaná. Like their neighbours they lost most of their land to ranching and tannin companies in the late 1800s and early 1900s. See also Toba-Lengua.
